target_customer: Hospitals and critical care physicians treating sepsis, ARDS and immune driven illness, plus pharma partners that license assets
problem: Critically ill patients with sepsis or ARDS are treated as one group although their immune responses differ, so trials of single therapies fail. Endpoint aimed to match therapies to patient biology with companion tests.
business_model: Precision therapeutics developer pairing licensed drugs with companion diagnostics and AI

founders.name: Diego Rey
education: UC Santa Barbara, BS electrical engineering

technical_complexity.rationale: Developing and trialing therapies for sepsis and ARDS together with companion immune response tests and AI needs clinical trials and regulatory approval, far beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed assets such as Grifols Antithrombin III and trial data could create a position, but the lead drug was an existing drug repurposed, limiting IP strength.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Grifols became a licensing partner in 2022 rather than a rival. No source shows an incumbent copying the precision sepsis wedge.

market_need_then: Sepsis and ARDS have high mortality and many failed trials of single therapies; COVID-19 in 2020 raised attention on immune driven critical illness, and the company launched publicly in July 2020 to bring personalized treatment to COVID-19 patients.

branding.domain_note: Uses endpointhealth.com, which now redirects to a GoDaddy hosted site.

identity.logo: Exists on directories but no source describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission statements about the right patient at the right time

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press covered the 2020 launch and 2022 Series A, but no source shows the brand itself driving anything. The name is generic and shared with other health and IT firms.

outcome_analysis: Endpoint Health came out of stealth in July 2020 with 12 million dollars, then raised a 52 million dollar Series A in June 2022 alongside a Grifols license for Antithrombin III in sepsis, a Phase II candidate. The YC page and Altss list it as inactive, Dealroom reports team size down 30 percent, and the website now redirects to a GoDaddy site, but no shutdown notice, layoff report or acquisition was found. The cause of any failure is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: The 2020 round is labeled 12 million dollars of debt and equity by BioWorld and the press release snippet, so stage is other. The Business Wire pages returned 403 and were read through search snippets. CB Insights lists a Series A II of 25M on 2022-06-02 and 77M across five rounds, conflicting with the 52M Series A at Seedtable and press; the rounds before 2020 are not found, so the gap is open. YC page status is Inactive while another snapshot showed Active, and the exit type is unknown. Founders Osborn, Springs and Teixeira have no sourced backgrounds. Competitors: Inflammatix (diagnostic only) appears only in 2020 aggregator results, too late and undated for the W19 batch, so the list is left empty.
